findings.finding: Unbounded payload columns in the new table: `sensitivity JSONB`, `inputs_snapshot JSONB` and `reasons TEXT[]` have no size limit at the DB level. The migration is otherwise sound (no secrets, taxonomy CHECKs on growth_confidence/wacc_confidence/wacc_source/valuation_status/valuation_confidence/graham_*/dcf_*, `> 0` CHECKs on all six scenarios, valuation_components BETWEEN 0 AND 4, UNIQUE (security_id, as_of, model_version), FK to securities(id), plus ck_valuation_results_has_value which forbids value-less rows). No user-controlled write path exists in M6b: the only writer is the pipeline (internal/pipeline/valuation.go -> storage.UpsertValuationResult) and its content is engine-generated and bounded (3x3 grid per axis by VALUATION_SENSITIVITY_STEPS, a ~20-field typed snapshot, and the fixed reason constants of internal/valuation/valuation.go). No endpoint accepts a body that reaches these columns. Abuse would therefore require a future mutating endpoint or a user-supplied concept/ticker list reaching the writer.
findings.recommended_fix: No change required for M6b. When the first endpoint that can influence these payloads is added, add a guard (e.g. CHECK (octet_length(sensitivity::text) <= 65536) AND octet_length(inputs_snapshot::text) <= 65536) or document the invariant that only engine-generated payloads may be persisted.

findings.finding: envFloat/envInt accept non-finite input: strconv.ParseFloat succeeds on "NaN", "Inf" and "+Inf", so VALUATION_BEAR_WACC_DELTA=NaN, MARGIN_OF_SAFETY=Inf or DCF_DISCOUNT_RATE=NaN are accepted SILENTLY (no slog.Warn, unlike an unparseable string) and enter Config. The engine is hardened downstream — sane() (internal/valuation/valuation.go:347) and isFinite() (internal/valuation/valuation.go:358) funnel every formula result and turn NaN/Inf into nil + the `non_finite` reason, and calcMOS/CalcUncertainty/CalcPEG re-check with isFinite — so today the failure mode is 'every valuation silently unavailable', not corruption or panic. Residual risk: PostgreSQL NUMERIC accepts 'NaN' and evaluates `NaN > 0` as TRUE, so any future numeric column NOT funneled through sane()/isFinite() could persist a NaN and pass the `> 0` CHECKs of migration 014. Requires operator misconfiguration (env var), not remote input.
findings.recommended_fix: Harden envFloat/envInt: after parsing, reject non-finite values (math.IsNaN/math.IsInf) with the existing slog.Warn + default path, so a bad env var is visible in the logs instead of silently degrading every row. Alternatively add the isFinite guard at the ConfigFromEnv boundary for the four reused env vars (MARGIN_OF_SAFETY, DCF_HORIZON_YEARS, DCF_TERMINAL_GROWTH, DCF_DISCOUNT_RATE, GROWTH_RATE_DEFAULT, WACC_FALLBACK).

findings.finding: The `integration` recipe prints the full test DSN to stdout in both the success and the failure branch: `echo "==> integración contra BD de test: $(TEST_DATABASE_URL)"` and the ERROR branch repeats it. The DSN shape used by this project embeds credentials (postgres://abys:abys@localhost:55432/abys_test per .env.example:16, deploy/setup.sh:141), so a real TEST_DATABASE_URL with a password would land in the terminal and in CI logs. PRE-EXISTING (already present at HEAD 7b68aed); M6b only touches the neighbouring line (TEST_DATABASE_URL=$$TEST_DATABASE_URL -> '$(TEST_DATABASE_URL)'), which actually FIXES the pre-existing F1 of abys-m52-health (empty propagation to the sub-make caused the integration suite to pass green with 0 tests). No secret value from the working tree (.env) was read during the scan.
findings.recommended_fix: Echo only the non-secret part of the DSN (e.g. host/port/database, or `${TEST_DATABASE_URL%%\?*}` with the userinfo stripped) so the guard message proves the *_test suffix without printing credentials. Low urgency: operator-controlled value, dev/test credentials.

findings.finding: The slog.Warn of a rejected env var includes the raw value (`"value", v`). Not a secret exposure today: every key read by ConfigFromEnv is numeric or boolean by contract (VALUATION_* deltas/steps, MARGIN_OF_SAFETY, DCF_*, GROWTH_RATE_DEFAULT, WACC_FALLBACK) and none can carry a credential. Recorded as a pattern to keep out of this function rather than as a defect.
findings.recommended_fix: No change required. If a string-valued key is ever parsed here, log the key only (or a truncated value).

findings.finding: .env.example is UNCHANGED by M6b while the milestone introduces 9 new env knobs read by valuation.ConfigFromEnv (VALUATION_BEAR_GROWTH_DELTA, VALUATION_BULL_GROWTH_DELTA, VALUATION_BEAR_WACC_DELTA, VALUATION_BULL_WACC_DELTA, VALUATION_BEAR_TERMINAL_DELTA, VALUATION_BULL_TERMINAL_DELTA, VALUATION_GROWTH_TRANSITION, VALUATION_GROWTH_TRANSITION_CAP, VALUATION_SENSITIVITY_STEPS), documented only in code comments (config.go:100-124). Impact is discoverability, not safety: absent env vars fall back to the defaults (confirmed tolerant parsing: envFloat/envInt/envBool return the default on empty or unparseable input, and ConfigFromEnv clamps HorizonYears<=0 and SensitivitySteps<1 — never panics, never errors). MARGIN_OF_SAFETY reuse is CONFIRMED: present in .env.example:65 and read at config.go:137. No new VALUATION_* entry leaks a value or credential anywhere.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a commented VALUATION_* block (names + default, no values) to .env.example next to MARGIN_OF_SAFETY, or defer to M6c together with the Parameter Sets (§24/§25) which will need the same block.

findings.finding: A 14.9 MB non-stripped Go ELF binary sits untracked at the repository root (identical Go BuildID to bin/analytics) and is NOT covered by .gitignore, which ignores only /bin/. Excluded from the source scan as instructed; it carries no secret material, but it is a commit accident waiting to happen (binary blob in product history).
findings.recommended_fix: Remove it (`make clean`) and add `/analytics` to .gitignore, or build exclusively into bin/ (the Makefile already targets bin/). Owner: git-manager/miky; no Git mutation performed by this scan.

findings.finding: tool_missing: gitleaks, gosec and govulncheck are not installed on this host (`which` returned only npm/node/go). Secret detection therefore used the documented regex fallback, which the skill classifies as ADVISORY and not as proof of absence. Mitigation applied instead: full read of migrations/014_create_valuation_results.sql, plus manual review of every changed/new Go and TSX file. `go vet` over internal/valuation, internal/storage, internal/pipeline, internal/api, internal/score, internal/growth and cmd/... returned clean (no findings).
findings.recommended_fix: Install gitleaks (and optionally gosec) as a setup concern outside the task, then re-run this scan to replace the advisory regex evidence with a real secret scan.

checks.migration_014: read in full (80 lines): no secrets; idempotent CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS + CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS; taxonomy CHECKs on every status/confidence and on wacc_source (5 values); `> 0` CHECKs on all six scenarios; valuation_components BETWEEN 0 AND 4; UNIQUE (security_id, as_of, model_version); FK security_id -> securities(id); ck_valuation_results_has_value prevents value-less rows; no identifier comes from user input (all identifiers are literals in the file).
checks.sql_injection: clean — no dynamic SQL in the new code. storage/valuation.go is 100% parameterized ($1..$37 + now() for calculation_timestamp); fundamentals.go builds SQL only by concatenating placeholder indices ($n) of an internal counter, never a user value; health.go's buildCountQuery interpolates only the hardcoded healthTableNames list, filtered by healthTableNameRe and qualified with public. No credentials, DSNs, internal hostnames or stack traces in any payload. loader.go degrades gracefully on an unreadable inputs_snapshot/sensitivity (warn + column projection) instead of failing the request.
checks.authz_and_authn: unchanged — no authentication/authorization model was added, removed or weakened by M6b; POST /refresh keeps its existing guardPipeline advisory-lock behaviour (409 on concurrent job).
checks.sql_parameterization_and_input: clean — GetSecurityByTicker/path params and all query filters use placeholders; the new GetLatestFYFundamentalsAsOf is fully parameterized ($1 security_id, $2 concept = ANY[], $3 asOf) and adds a look-ahead guard (filing_date <= asOf), which is an integrity improvement.
checks.dependencies: UNCHANGED — `git diff --stat 7b68aed -- go.mod go.sum web/package.json web/package-lock.json package.json package-lock.json` is empty and `git status --short` shows no modification/untracked entry for any of them. M6b introduces zero new third-party dependencies (new imports are limited to encoding/json, errors, log/slog, math, time and the already-present github.com/jackc/pgx/v5). The only parsing gap is the non-finite case of SEC-M6b-002.

methodology.notes: M6b is a pure-valuation milestone with no new routes, no new dependencies and no credential surface. The new table is taxonomy-constrained at the DB level and every write path is parameterized and engine-generated. The two low findings are hardening opportunities (unbounded JSONB payload columns, non-finite env values) and one pre-existing low finding on the Makefile DSN echo whose neighbouring line M6b actually fixes. No policy-defined hard block (exposed secret) is present, so M6b may proceed to Review.

summary: Security scan M6b abys-m6b-valuation: VERDICT pass, 0 hard blocks, 7 findings (2 low, 5 info), all advisory. No secrets in the 5194-line diff or the 7 new internal/valuation files, internal/pipeline/valuation.go, internal/storage/valuation.go and migration 014 (regex fallback = advisory; gitleaks/gosec/govulncheck tool_missing). Zero dependency changes: go.mod, go.sum and web/package-lock.json are untouched, so no new supply-chain surface and no dependency audit applicable. Migration 014 has no secrets, constrains every status/confidence with CHECKs, blocks value-less rows and takes no identifier from user input. No dynamic SQL: all writes/reads are parameterized; health.go still interpolates only the hardcoded, regex-filtered table list (valuation_results added). No new API routes (router.go unchanged) and no new sensitive response fields; POST /refresh only gains an additive `valuation` counter. Frontend adds no dangerous sinks, external URLs or secret usage. New VALUATION_* env vars parse tolerantly without panic (defaults + warn, clamped ranges); the only gap is that ParseFloat accepts NaN/Inf silently, contained downstream by sane()/isFinite(). go vet clean. Hygiene: untracked 14.9 MB ./analytics ELF binary at the repo root is not covered by .gitignore (excluded from the scan, no secret material).
